title: Archie catch-up
logline: Archie, still jumpy since Whitechapel, finds out you can make the thing he lost, and pays for that in his own way: calc he can't stand to touch, and a pearl he won't take if it's your only one.
questions: Existing art (card1/4/8) shows Archie STANDING in the aisle with his phone. The proposal has him sat with his back to a pillar at a table ('He's sat like that', 'on the table between you'). Recommend: new seated plate, retire all three old images. Keep any?

The proposal pins card1/card4/card8 as explicit image keys. On promotion those pins should go (discovery by position), or be re-pointed at the new files. Decide at implement time; noted so the old images don't shadow the new ones.
S4 (foot nudges the bag) needs a second camera: a floor-level plate (P2). It's the allergy beat and the moment the calc changes hands. Spend it, or cut S4 and HOLD S1 at c8 (saves a plate + a shot)?

Calc in the bag: show a few dull-gold rough stones in the open mouth of the bag (ART-BIBLE accent gold), or keep the bag knotted shut? There's no canon for what raw calc looks like, so the board keeps it shut for now.

Bin shot (S5): frozen instant = wrapper just dropping into a bin at screen-right, Archie's arm still out from the throw, his eyes already back on the aisle. The bus line on the same card is text only. OK?
No hand of yours on screen anywhere (pure POV, no sprite). OK, or add a sleeve/hand withdrawing from the pearl in S2?

cards.text: Archie is eating a falafel wrap with his back to a pillar, where he can see both ends of the aisle. He's sat like that since Whitechapel. He waves you over.
cards.why: New location. The pillar and the two ends of the aisle are the tell, so the set itself carries the hook.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "Go on, then. How'd it go with James? He have you sweeping up, or did he let you near the good stuff?"
You think about the bench, the ledger, and what's in your pocket.
cards.why: Choice card: no pearl in frame, so neither option is given away. The offer result text plays over S1 too; the pearl shows up on the next card.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: He looks at the pearl, then at your pocket, which clinks. "How many have you got?" You tell him. He breathes out. "Then I'll have that one. Next time someone gets a knife out, I'd like a better answer than running."
cards.why: The pearl lands. Gold accent in the middle of the table, Archie leaning back from it with his eyes running but still looking at it. Want and allergy in one frame.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "That your only one?" He pushes it back across the table with one finger, eyes still running. "Keep it on you. Nights especially. Give me the next one you make."
cards.why: The turn of the event on this path: care that costs him. A closer shot of one finger pushing the pearl back to camera. Different action from S2, so it can't share S2's image.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "James doesn't show people things. James does things, judges you for not knowing how, and considers that a complete interaction." He tilts his head. "So either he was desperate, or he saw something worth the bother. Don't let it go to your head."
cards.why: Return to S1 (free). Must be NEW: both pearl paths arrive here with a pearl image showing that is now wrong (he pocketed it, or you took it back). On the vague path it just looks like a hold.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "Keep practising. Make your own and you're not paying James's prices, which are a war crime. And there's buyers for finished pearls, same as the calc. Anything you don't need, bring it to me. We split it down the middle."
cards.why: Pitch talk in the same moment.

cards.text: He nudges a carrier bag across the floor to you with his foot, without touching it. "Twenty units of time calc. Was going to line up a buyer for it, but if you can turn it into pearls we'll make a lot more. Practise on that."
cards.why: Decisive physical action plus a new prop: the calc changes hands. The foot is the joke and the allergy, so it's an insert at floor level.

cards.text: He finishes his wrap and bins the wrapper from four metres away. It goes in first time. He doesn't acknowledge this at all. You take the bag home on your lap, which feels like a lot of calc for one bus.
cards.why: Closing gag. Frozen just after the wrapper goes in: arm still out, eyes already back on the aisle. That's the 'doesn't acknowledge it' and the tell together.

plates.name: spitalfields_pillar
plates.camera: Seated POV across a small café table, looking at the empty chair opposite, backed against a cast-iron pillar, with the aisle running off both sides
plates.prompt:
Attach: archie_craft_chat_card1.png.
A blank background plate for a pixel-art game scene: inside Old Spitalfields Market, East London, late afternoon on a weekday, dry. The same market as archie_craft_chat_card1.png: Victorian cast-iron columns and a glazed iron roof, red-brick buildings, green stall awnings, strings of warm festoon bulbs.
Camera: seated eye height, about 1.2 m, normal lens, looking straight across a small round dark-metal café table at the empty chair opposite.
Set: the near table edge runs along the bottom of the frame; the tabletop is empty and clean. Opposite, centred, a simple metal café chair with its back right up against a thick green-black cast-iron pillar. Behind it, the market aisle runs left to right across the frame, and both ends of the aisle are visible, receding: screen-left, a falafel stall under a green awning with festoon bulbs; screen-right, a clothes rail stall with white canopy. Screen-right midground, about four metres from the chair, a black metal litter bin standing on its own on the paving. Paving tiles, a few wooden crates. The glazed roof and iron trusses fill the top of the frame.
Light: soft daylight through the glazed roof from above, slightly cool. Warm festoon bulbs along both stalls.
Genuine pixel art: visible pixel grid with roughly 4×4 screen pixels per art pixel, limited palette, dithered shading, crisp hard edges, no anti-aliasing, no painterly blur, no vector/cel-shaded linework. Match the pixel-art technique and colour treatment of archie_craft_chat_card1.png.
Grounded, realistic London colour: brick, shopfront paint, wet pavement, sodium and LED light. Vivid where the real city is, restrained elsewhere. No neon, no fantasy glow.
Portrait 2:3 (1024×1536), full-bleed, no border. No people, not even distant background figures (extras are added per shot). No text, letters, numbers or logos: signs and stall boards show shapes only.
Keep the chair, the tabletop and the bin in the middle band of the frame; the top and bottom 15% may be cropped, so only roof and table edge go there.
plates.notes: Lights: roof daylight (cool white, overhead, 1.0); festoon bulbs (warm, both stalls, 0.4). Occluders: the table, in front of anyone seated opposite; the pillar behind the chair. Bin screen-right is S5's target. 180°: Archie always centre, the bin always screen-right.

plates.name: spitalfields_pillar_floor
plates.camera: Floor-level insert under the table edge, looking along the paving at the foot of the chair opposite and the pillar base
plates.prompt:
Attach: spitalfields_pillar_blank_plate.png, archie_craft_chat_card1.png.
A blank background plate for a pixel-art game scene: the same corner of Old Spitalfields Market as spitalfields_pillar_blank_plate.png, seen from a new camera.
Camera: very low, about 30 cm off the floor, under the near edge of the small round café table, looking along the paving tiles toward the chair opposite. The dark-metal table's central leg and the underside of its top frame the upper part of the shot.
Set: midground, centred, the legs of the empty metal café chair, and behind them the base of the thick green-black cast-iron pillar. Clear paving tiles between the camera and the chair, where something will be slid along the floor. Background, out of focus: the bottoms of stall tables and crates, festoon-bulb glow, the aisle floor running away both sides.
Light: soft daylight from above, the table casting a shadow over the near floor; warm bulb glow in the background.
Genuine pixel art: visible pixel grid with roughly 4×4 screen pixels per art pixel, limited palette, dithered shading, crisp hard edges, no anti-aliasing, no painterly blur, no vector/cel-shaded linework. Match the pixel-art technique and colour treatment of archie_craft_chat_card1.png.
Grounded, realistic London colour: brick, shopfront paint, wet pavement, sodium and LED light. Vivid where the real city is, restrained elsewhere. No neon, no fantasy glow.
Portrait 2:3 (1024×1536), full-bleed, no border. No people, no feet, not even distant background figures. No text, letters, numbers or logos.
Keep the floor between the camera and the chair clear in the middle band of the frame; the top and bottom 15% may be cropped.
plates.notes: Lights: daylight (overhead, 0.8), bulb glow (warm, background, 0.3). Occluders: the table leg and top. A separate camera from P1, not a variant.

shots.title: Back to the pillar
shots.job: Establish Archie as he is now: eating, friendly, sitting where nobody can come up behind him.
shots.prompt:
Attach: spitalfields_pillar_blank_plate.png, Archie_biz_sprite_master.png.
Using the market in spitalfields_pillar_blank_plate.png, add the man from Archie_biz_sprite_master.png sitting on the chair opposite, centre, his back right against the pillar, body square to the camera. He's holding a half-eaten falafel wrap in paper in one hand at chest height. His face is relaxed and friendly, but his eyes have slid sideways toward the screen-left end of the aisle, checking it. His other hand rests on the table.
Background extras, small and soft: a few shoppers at both ends of the aisle, a stallholder at the falafel stall screen-left.
Same pixel-art style and scale as the room. Change nothing else in the room. Keep the exact image size.
shots.unseen: Any pearl, any calc, the carrier bag (it's on the floor under the table, out of shot).

shots.title: Pearl on the table
shots.job: The thing he lost in Whitechapel is back on the table, and his body pulls away from it while his eyes don't.
shots.prompt:
Attach: spitalfields_pillar_blank_plate.png, Archie_biz_sprite_master.png, spitalfields_pillar_S1_archie_back_to_pillar.png, timePearl.png.
Using the market in spitalfields_pillar_blank_plate.png, add the man from Archie_biz_sprite_master.png in the chair opposite (as in spitalfields_pillar_S1_archie_back_to_pillar.png), now leaning back hard against the pillar, away from the table. His eyes are red and streaming, but he's staring at the middle of the table. The wrap is forgotten in his lowered hand.
In the exact centre of the table: one small pearl like timePearl.png, pale and pearlescent in a thin gold setting, about the size of a marble. It is the only warm gold note in the frame. No glow or sparkle.
Background extras, small and soft: shoppers at the aisle ends, unaware.
Same pixel-art style and scale as the room. Change nothing else in the room. Keep the exact image size.
shots.unseen: Your hand, other pearls, the carrier bag.

shots.title: Pushed back
shots.job: He won't take your only one. The kindness is in one finger.
shots.prompt:
Attach: spitalfields_pillar_blank_plate.png, Archie_biz_sprite_master.png, spitalfields_pillar_S1_archie_back_to_pillar.png, timePearl.png.
Using the market in spitalfields_pillar_blank_plate.png, add the man from Archie_biz_sprite_master.png in the chair opposite (as in spitalfields_pillar_S1_archie_back_to_pillar.png), leaning forward over the table with one arm stretched out, his face turned slightly away and his eyes red and streaming. One fingertip is pushing a small pearl like timePearl.png (pale, pearlescent, thin gold setting, marble-sized) across the table toward the camera; the pearl is on the near half of the table, close to the camera. His expression is firm and a bit gruff: he's looking you in the eye. The wrap is in his other hand.
Background extras, small and soft: shoppers at the aisle ends.
Same pixel-art style and scale as the room. Change nothing else in the room. Keep the exact image size.
shots.unseen: Your hand. No glow on the pearl.

shots.title: Foot on the bag
shots.job: Twenty units of calc changes hands, and Archie won't touch it with anything but his trainer.
shots.prompt:
Attach: spitalfields_pillar_floor_blank_plate.png, Archie_biz_sprite_master.png, spoons_table_S7_archie_eyes_streaming.png.
Using the floor in spitalfields_pillar_floor_blank_plate.png, add the dark jeans and white trainers of the man from Archie_biz_sprite_master.png, seated in the chair opposite (seen only from the knees down). One leg is stretched out along the paving: the toe of his trainer is pushing a white plastic carrier bag (the same kind of bag as in spoons_table_S7_archie_eyes_streaming.png) across the floor toward the camera. The bag is heavy, lumpy and knotted shut at the handles, sitting in the middle of the frame. His other foot is pulled well back under the chair.
Same pixel-art style and scale as the room. Change nothing else in the room. Keep the exact image size.
shots.unseen: Archie's face or hands. What's inside the bag (see open question).

shots.title: Nothing but net
shots.job: The closing gag: a perfect shot, and he's already watching the aisle again.
shots.prompt:
Attach: spitalfields_pillar_blank_plate.png, Archie_biz_sprite_master.png, spitalfields_pillar_S1_archie_back_to_pillar.png.
Using the market in spitalfields_pillar_blank_plate.png, add the man from Archie_biz_sprite_master.png in the chair opposite (as in spitalfields_pillar_S1_archie_back_to_pillar.png), back against the pillar, his throwing arm still stretched out toward the litter bin screen-right just after a throw. A balled-up paper wrapper is dropping cleanly into the bin's opening. He is not watching it: his head is turned the other way, eyes on the screen-left end of the aisle, face completely deadpan. The table in front of him is empty.

Same pixel-art style and scale as the room. Change nothing else in the room. Keep the exact image size.
